title: Line Graph Sequence
statementMd:
In the mathematical discipline of graph theory, the line graph of a simple undirected graph 𝐺G is another simple undirected graph 𝐿(𝐺)L(G) that represents the adjacency between every two edges in 𝐺G.

Precisely speaking, for an undirected graph 𝐺G without self-loops or multiple edges, its line graph 𝐿(𝐺)L(G) is a graph such that

- each vertex of 𝐿(𝐺)L(G) represents an edge of 𝐺G; and
- two vertices of 𝐿(𝐺)L(G) are adjacent if and only if their corresponding edges share a common endpoint in 𝐺G.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/9931c197160febaeb1da1ce82758002deefc92df.png) Figure: Generation of the Line Graph

Given a simple undirected graph 𝐺G, you need to find the minimum number of vertices among all the graphs in sequence 𝐿0(𝐺),𝐿1(𝐺),…,𝐿𝑘−1(𝐺)L0(G),L1(G),…,Lk−1(G), where 𝐿0(𝐺)=𝐺L0(G)=G and 𝐿𝑡(𝐺)=𝐿(𝐿𝑡−1(𝐺))Lt(G)=L(Lt−1(G)) for each positive integer 𝑡t.

## Input

The input contains several test cases, and the first line contains a single integer 𝑇T (1≤𝑇≤1051≤T≤105), denoting the number of test cases.

For each test case:

The first line contains three integers 𝑛n (1≤𝑛≤1051≤n≤105), 𝑚m (0≤𝑚≤min(𝑛(𝑛−1)2,105)0≤m≤min(n(n−1)2,105))), and 𝑘k (1≤𝑘≤1051≤k≤105), denoting the number of vertices and edges in graph 𝐺G and the length of the line graph sequence.

Then 𝑚m lines follow, each of which contains two integers 𝑢u and 𝑣v (1≤𝑢,𝑣≤𝑛1≤u,v≤n), denoting an undirected edge connecting the 𝑢u-th and the 𝑣v-th vertices in graph 𝐺G. It is guaranteed that graph 𝐺G contains no self-loops or multiple edges.

It is guaranteed that the total number of vertices and edges in all test cases do not exceed 105105 respectively.

## Output

For each test case, output a line containing a single integer, indicating the minimum number of vertices among all the graphs in the sequence 𝐿0(𝐺),𝐿1(𝐺),…,𝐿𝑘−1(𝐺)L0(G),L1(G),…,Lk−1(G).
